disease_label_per_paper: Septic abortion resulting from beta-lactamase-negative ampicillin-resistant non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae infection
presentation_summary: 31-year-old previously healthy gravida 2 para 1 woman presented at 17 weeks and 6 days gestation with high fever and rigors.
Before presentation she had mild cough for 9 days, light vaginal bleeding with lower abdominal pain for 4 days, and was admitted as threatened premature delivery.
Despite tocolytic treatment she aborted spontaneously 2 hours after admission and then entered septic shock.
At transfer she was systemically unwell but fully aware; abdomen was soft, mildly distended, and not sore to touch.
Vital signs showed blood pressure 75/49 mmHg, heart rate 122/min, temperature 39.1 C, respiratory rate 17/min, and oxygen saturation 99% while receiving oxygen by face mask at 10 L/min.
Transabdominal ultrasound detected only a small amount of endometrial cavity fluid and no ascites; speculum exam showed neither significant bleeding nor purulent discharge from the cervical os.

Labs showed CRP 6.0 mg/dL, procalcitonin 20.45 ng/mL, WBC 4.4 x10^9/L, platelets 11 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 90 g/L, normal PT and aPTT, elevated FDP and d-dimer suggesting pre-DIC, and normal kidney and liver function.

quality_warnings: Blood/vaginal culture identity and susceptibility are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Septic shock, recent spontaneous abortion, fever/rigors, lower abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding history, thrombocytopenia, CRP/PCT, and pre-DIC context are ranking evidence.
Haemophilus influenzae is represented as microbiology/treatment context, not a disease-name qualifier.
